paragraphs: We are a clinical-stage biotechnology company developing precision therapies to treat solid tumors designed to preserve organ function. Our lead candidate bel-sar is in late-stage clinical development for the treatment of patients with early choroidal melanoma (defined as small choroidal melanoma and/or indeterminate lesions) and is also in clinical development for other ocular oncology indications and bladder cancer.

There is significant unmet need for novel treatments for patients with choroidal melanoma, given the limitations of the current standard of care, or SoC, and patient reluctance to undergo radiotherapy in the form of either plaque brachytherapy or proton beam therapy, both highly-invasive therapies that result in significant vision loss, and potential legal blindness in the treated eye. Enucleation, or surgical removal of the affected eye, is another treatment option for patients with choroidal melanoma, in which patients lose all vision without the possibility of vision restoration. We are evaluating the safety and efficacy of bel-sar as a potential vision-sparing therapy in our ongoing global Phase 3 CoMpass trial for the first-line treatment of adult patients with early choroidal melanoma. Moreover, we intend to assess the safety and efficacy of bel-sar in treating a range of other solid tumors, beginning with metastases to the choroid and bladder cancer where bel-sar is in clinical development, as well as in cancers of the ocular surface. We believe bel-sar, if approved, has the potential to change the current treatment paradigm for patients with ocular and urologic cancers and other solid tumors.

Bel-sar has shown clinical benefit and has been generally well-tolerated in clinical trials to date. In a Phase 2 study (ClinicalTrials.gov ID: NCT04417530) evaluating suprachoroidal, or SC, administration of bel-sar for the first-line treatment of early choroidal melanoma, patients were closely monitored over a twelve-month follow-up period to assess tumor control, visual acuity preservation, and tumor growth rate. A total of 22 patients were enrolled in the study. Bel-sar achieved an 80% tumor control rate (n=8/10) among Phase 3-eligible patients who received the therapeutic regimen, with complete cessation of growth following treatment among responders (post-treatment average growth rate of 0.011 mm/yr among responders compared to 0.351 mm/yr prior to study entry; p<0.0001). Visual acuity preservation was achieved in 90% of these ten patients. Importantly, 80% of these ten patients were at high risk for vision loss with tumors close to the fovea or optic disc, highlighting the potential for vision preservation with this novel class of drugs. The safety profile of bel-sar was highly favorable in all participants regardless of dose. We believe the Phase 2 results are a significant achievement considering the typically poor prognosis associated with choroidal melanoma, a rare and life-threatening ocular cancer, where there are no approved vision-preserving therapies to date. We believe bel-sar has the possibility to transform the field of ocular oncology beyond choroidal melanoma and we are expanding clinical development in two additional indications: metastases to the choroid and cancers of the ocular surface. We continue to enroll patients in an ongoing Phase 2 clinical trial in metastases to the choroid and we are initiating a Phase 1 proof-of-concept trial in cancers of the ocular surface.

Virus-like drug conjugates, or VDCs, are a novel class of drugs with a dual mechanism of action that promote cancer cell death by both the delivery of the cytotoxic payload to generate acute necrosis and activation of a secondary immune mediated response. Bel-sar, our lead VDC candidate, consists of modified capsid proteins of the human papilloma virus, or HPV, conjugated to hundreds of light-activated molecules.

Light activation of bel-sar is designed to result in precise tumor cell killing with minimal damage to surrounding healthy tissues. In the absence of bel-sar activation or binding to the tumor cell membrane, there is no cytotoxic effect. Multiple light activations, following a single dose of bel-sar, increase antitumor activity because of the reoxygenation of the tumor and the photostability of bel-sar. Finally, acute necrosis triggers immunogenic cell death leading to the generation of an adaptive, long-term antitumor immune response. The tumor targeting specificity of VDCs is driven by the selective binding of the virus-like particles, or VLPs, to a subset of modified tumor associated glycosaminoglycans, or GAGs, that are part of the heparan sulphate chain of heparan sulfate proteoglycans or HSPGs, expressed on the tumor cell membrane. This targeting mechanism enables the delivery of multiple types of cytotoxic payloads directly to a wide range of solid tumors.

Beyond ocular cancers, bel-sar is in clinical development in bladder cancer. Bladder cancer is the ninth most common cancer worldwide and the majority of cases are diagnosed early as non-muscle invasive bladder cancer, or NMIBC, with a prevalence of approximately 80,000 cases per year in the United States. Despite the early diagnosis, patients with NMIBC have a high risk of recurrence and progression with current SoC treatments. In 2025, we announced positive data from our Phase 1 trial in NMIBC (NCT05483868). Based on the positive results from the completed Phase 1 trial, we are advancing the clinical development of bel-sar in NMIBC. We have an ongoing Phase 1b/2 trial in NMIBC evaluating additional doses and cycles in intermediate and high-risk NMIBC patients.

Our vision is to innovate the future of cancer care to cure patients and preserve organ function. We are developing bel-sar in several indications in ocular oncology, with the goal of treating tumors, preserving vision and preventing blindness in patients. Our lead indication is a potential multi-billion dollar addressable market opportunity. We are also evaluating bel-sar in urologic oncology indications, initially in bladder cancer, which is one of the most expensive cancers to treat on a per patient basis. The global market for bladder cancer is expected to be greater than $8.0 billion by 2032.
Our initial focus is in ocular and urologic oncology, both areas of high unmet medical need where local targeted therapies may enable early intervention, as shown in our pipeline below.

We envision the potential for development of other oncology therapeutic areas in addition to ocular and urologic cancers.

Our management team includes industry executives with extensive biopharmaceutical experience in developing and commercializing drugs in oncology and ophthalmology. Elisabet de los Pinos, Ph.D., our Chief Executive Officer, led the marketing strategy and European commercialization of Alimta® for the treatment of lung cancer at Eli Lilly and Company. Our Chief Medical Officer and President of Research & Development, J. Jill Hopkins, M.D., is an ophthalmologist and retinal specialist with more than 30 years of experience in ophthalmology, including serving as Senior Vice President, Global Head of Ophthalmology and Exploratory Development at Novartis AG, or Novartis, and Chief Executive Officer of Gyroscope Therapeutics, a Novartis company, where she was responsible for the global ophthalmic pipeline. Anthony Gibney, our Chief Financial and Business Officer, is an experienced biotechnology leader and former investment banker who brings over 30 years of experience dedicated to leading and advising biotechnology companies across their businesses, including corporate strategy, business development, finance and investor relations, among others. Following his investment banking career, he has worked as Chief Business Officer at Achillion Pharmaceuticals, Inc. and Iveric Bio, Inc. and as Chief Business and Financial Officer at Fog Pharmaceuticals, Inc. Conor Kilroy, our Chief Legal Officer and Secretary, served as general counsel and secretary at Neurogastrx, Inc. from September 2021 to May 2023. Mr. Kilroy also served in roles of increasing responsibility at Ironwood Pharmaceuticals, Inc. (Nasdaq: IRWD) from June 2013 to February 2021, serving as senior vice president, general counsel and secretary beginning in April 2020 and vice president, general counsel and secretary beginning in April 2019. Earlier in his career, Mr. Kilroy held roles at Boston Scientific Corporation and in the business law department of Goodwin Procter LLP. Mark Plavsic, Ph.D. is our Chief Technology Officer and brings 30 years of global biopharmaceutical experience including end-to-end technical operations in the United States, Europe, and Australasia and successful translation and scale-up of complex biologics from preclinical development through commercial launch and distribution. He previously served as Chief Technology Officer at Fate Therapeutics, Inc. and at Lysogene. We believe the breadth and depth of experience amongst our management team will enable us to advance the clinical and development strategy for bel-sar and, if approved, its commercialization. Our Chairman of the Board of Directors, David Johnson, is a biopharmaceutical industry veteran with more than 25 years of experience in drug development. Mr. Johnson is currently Chief Executive Officer and founder of Solve Therapeutics, Inc., a biotechnology company developing next-generation mAb-based oncology therapeutics. Prior to founding Solve Therapeutics, he was Chief Executive Officer of VelosBio Inc., an oncology company acquired by Merck & Co. for $2.75 billion in 2020. He was also Chief Executive Officer at Acerta Pharma, which was acquired by AstraZeneca for $7 billion. Mr. Johnson has extensive experience leading the development of first-in-class cancer therapies and has made significant contributions to drugs which ultimately garnered regulatory approvals, including bortezomib (Velcade®), romidepsin (Istodax®), idelalisib (Zydelig®), and acalabrutinib (Calquence®).

At Aura Biosciences, our vision is to innovate the future of cancer care to cure patients and preserve organ function, with an initial focus on ocular and urologic oncology. Key elements of our strategy to accomplish this objective include:

▪ Complete the ongoing global Phase 3 CoMpass trial of bel-sar as a first-line treatment of early choroidal melanoma and pursue U.S. Food and Drug Administration, or FDA, approval. If approved, this would represent the first therapy for early choroidal melanoma as a potential first-line treatment option, reserving radiotherapy for a second-line treatment option. If approved, we see the potential to independently commercialize bel-sar in choroidal melanoma, which has an incidence of 11,000 patients diagnosed per year in the United States and Europe. There are approximately 50 ocular oncologists in the United States and approximately 50 ocular oncologists in Europe, representing a focused call point and providing an opportunity for our company to capture the value of the market with a focused sales team globally.

▪ Expand the development of bel-sar in additional ocular oncology indications, including metastases to the choroid and cancers of the ocular surface. We believe bel-sar's dual mechanism of action has potential to treat tumors while preserving key ocular structures, in other ocular cancers that affect a large number of patients. We continue to enroll patients in the ongoing Phase 2 clinical trial in metastases to the choroid. Metastases to the choroid has an annual incidence rate of 20,000 patients in the United States and Europe. In addition, we plan to conduct a Phase 1 proof-of-concept trial of bel-sar for cancers of the ocular surface, including both melanomas and squamous cell carcinomas, that has an incidence rate of 35,000 patients a year in the United States and Europe, based on strong interest from the ocular oncology community to develop better treatment options for patients.

headings: Risks Related to Our Financial Position, and Additional Capital Needs

We have incurred significant net losses since our inception and anticipate that we will continue to incur losses for the foreseeable future, which raises a risk regarding our ability to continue as a going concern.
Our auditors have issued a "going concern" audit opinion.
Recent volatility in capital markets may affect our ability to access new capital through sales of shares of our common stock or issuance of indebtedness.
Raising additional capital may cause dilution to our existing stockholders, restrict our operations or require us to relinquish proprietary rights to our technologies or product candidates.
Risks Related to the Discovery and Development of our Product Candidates
We are heavily dependent on the success of bel-sar, our only product candidate to date.
We have initiated but not yet completed a pivotal clinical trial nor have we commercialized any pharmaceutical products, which may make it difficult to evaluate our future prospects.
If we fail to develop additional product candidates, or obtain additional indications of our first product candidate, our commercial opportunity could be limited.
Bel-sar is a biologic that requires the use of multiple medical devices, which may result in additional regulatory risks.
Changes in methods of product candidate manufacturing or formulation may result in additional costs or delay.
If we experience delays or difficulties in the enrollment of patients in clinical trials, our receipt of necessary regulatory approvals could be delayed or prevented.
The results of preclinical studies and early clinical trials may not be predictive of future results.
We may incur additional costs or experience delays in initiating or completing, or ultimately be unable to complete, the development and commercialization of our product candidates.
paragraphs: Investing in our common stock involves a high degree of risk. You should carefully read and consider all of the risks described below, as well as the other information in this Annual Report on Form 10-K, including our consolidated financial statements and related notes thereto and the section titled "Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations". The occurrence of any of the events or developments described below could harm our business, financial condition, results of operations and growth prospects. Unless otherwise indicated, references to our business being harmed in these risk factors will include harm to our business, reputation, financial condition, results of operations and future prospects. In such an event, the market price of our common stock could decline, and you may lose all or part of your investment. Additional risks and uncertainties not presently known to us or that we currently deem immaterial also may impair our business operations and the market price of our common stock.

Investment in biotechnology product development is highly speculative because it entails substantial upfront capital expenditures and significant risk that a product candidate will fail to gain regulatory approval or fail to become commercially viable. Our net losses were $106.2 million and $86.9 million for the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024, respectively. As of December 31, 2025, we had an accumulated deficit of $480.4 million. Substantially all of our net losses have resulted from costs incurred in connection with our research and development programs and from general and administrative costs associated with our operations. We expect our research and development expenses to increase significantly as we continue clinical development for bel-sar and continue to discover and develop additional product candidates. In addition, if we obtain regulatory approval for our product candidates, we will incur significant sales, marketing and manufacturing expenses. We incur costs, and will incur additional costs, associated with operating as a public company. As a result, we expect to continue to incur significant and increasing operating losses for the foreseeable future. Because of the numerous risks and uncertainties associated with developing pharmaceutical products, we are unable to predict the extent of any future losses or when we will become profitable, if at all. To date, we have not generated any revenue from any product sales. Our history of losses and no revenues creates a greater risk of our ability to continue as a going concern in the future. Our ability to become profitable depends upon our ability to generate revenue. We have no products approved for commercial sale and, therefore, have never generated any revenue from product sales, and we do not expect to in the foreseeable future. Further, we do not anticipate generating any revenue from product sales until after we have received marketing approval for the commercial sale of a product candidate, if ever. Our ability to generate revenue and achieve profitability depends significantly on our success in achieving a number of goals, including:

▪ initiating and completing research regarding, and preclinical and clinical development of, bel-sar in early choroidal melanoma and additional oncology indications, including metastases to the choroid and bladder cancer as well as any other research programs from our VDC technology platform and any future product candidates;
▪ obtaining marketing approval for bel-sar and any future product candidates for which we complete clinical trials;

▪ transferring our manufacturing process to, and developing and maintaining it with, a CDMO for bel-sar and any future product candidates, including establishing and maintaining commercially viable supply and manufacturing relationships with third parties;
▪ launching and commercializing bel-sar and any future product candidates for which we obtain marketing approvals, either directly or with a collaborator or distributor;

We were incorporated as a Delaware corporation in 2009 and our headquarters are located in Boston, Massachusetts. Since our inception, we have focused our efforts on identifying and developing potential product candidates, conducting preclinical studies and clinical trials, organizing and staffing our company, business planning, establishing and maintaining our intellectual property portfolio, raising capital, conducting discovery, research and development activities and providing general and administrative support for these operations. We do not have any product candidates approved for sale and have not generated any revenue to date. We have funded our operations primarily through the sale of convertible preferred stock, common stock, and warrants. From inception through December 31, 2025, we have raised an aggregate of approximately $498.1 million of gross proceeds primarily from private placements of our equity and convertible preferred stock as well as through the issuance of our common stock. On May 16, 2025, we issued and sold 11,735,565 shares of common stock, pre-funded warrants to purchase up to 3,571,435 shares of common stock, and accompanying warrants to purchase an aggregate of 3,826,750 shares of common stock, or the 2025 Follow-On Offering. The common stock and pre-funded warrants were sold in the 2025 Follow-On Offering in combination with an accompanying common stock warrant to purchase 0.25 of a share of common stock for each share of common stock or pre-funded warrant sold. Each such share of common stock was offered and sold together with an accompanying common stock warrant at a combined offering price of $4.90, and each such pre-funded warrant was offered and sold together with an accompanying common stock warrant at a combined offering price of $4.89999. We received approximately $69.9 million in net proceeds from the 2025 Follow-On Offering after deducting underwriting discounts and commissions and offering expenses. On November 9, 2023, we issued and sold 11,000,000 shares of common stock at a price to the public of $9.00 per share for aggregate gross proceeds of $99.0 million, or the 2023 Follow-On Offering. We received approximately $92.6 million in net proceeds from the 2023 Follow-On Offering after deducting underwriting discounts and commissions and offering expenses. On December 5, 2022, we issued and sold 7,705,000 shares of common stock, including the full exercise of the underwriters' option to purchase additional shares at a price to the public of $12.00 per share, for aggregate gross proceeds of $92.5 million, or the 2022 Follow-On Offering. We received approximately $86.7 million in net proceeds from the 2022 Follow-On Offering after deducting underwriting discounts, commissions and offering expenses. On November 1, 2022, we filed a shelf registration statement on Form S-3, or the 2022 Shelf, with the Securities and Exchange Commission, or the SEC, in relation to the registration of up to an aggregate offering price of $250.0 million of common stock, preferred stock, debt securities, warrants and units or any combination thereof. We also simultaneously entered into an Open Market Sale AgreementSM, or the Sales Agreement, with Jefferies LLC, or the Sales Agent, to provide for the offering, issuance and sale by us of up to an aggregate of $75.0 million of its common stock from time to time in "at-the-market" offerings, or the ATM, under the 2022 Shelf and subject to the limitations thereof. In connection with the 2023 Follow-On Offering, on November 6, 2023, we delivered written notice to Jefferies that we were suspending and terminating the prospectus related to the shares issuable in the ATM pursuant to the terms of the Sales Agreement. During the year ended December 31, 2023, we issued a total of 261,807 shares of common stock at a weighted average price of $12.49 for aggregate gross proceeds of $3.3 million under the ATM. On March 27, 2024, we filed a new shelf registration statement on Form S-3, or the 2024 Shelf, with the SEC in relation to the registration of up to an aggregate offering price of $350.0 million of common stock, preferred stock, debt securities, warrants and units or any combination thereof, which superseded the 2022 Shelf. The 2024 Shelf included a prospectus supplement to provide for offerings in the ATM under the Sales Agreement. We issued 1,055,362 shares of common stock at a weighted average price of $6.36 for aggregate gross proceeds of $6.7 million during the year ended December 31, 2025 under the ATM.

We have incurred significant operating losses in every year since our inception in 2009 and have not generated any revenue. We expect to continue to incur significant expenses and operating losses for the foreseeable future. Our ability to generate product revenue sufficient to achieve profitability will depend on the successful development and commercialization of one or more of our product candidates. Our net losses were $106.2 million and $86.9 million for the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024, respectively. As of December 31, 2025, we had an accumulated deficit of $480.4 million. In addition, our losses from operations may fluctuate significantly from quarter-to-quarter and year-to-year, depending on the timing of our clinical trials and our expenditures on other research and development activities.

We anticipate that our expenses and capital requirements will increase substantially in connection with our ongoing activities, particularly as we advance the preclinical studies and clinical trials of our product candidates. In addition, we incur additional costs associated with operating as a public company. We expect that our expenses and capital requirements will increase substantially if and as we:
▪ conduct our current and future clinical trials of bel-sar; ▪ progress the preclinical and clinical development of new indications;
▪ establish our manufacturing capability, including establishing and developing our contract development and manufacturing relationships;

paragraphs: 本公司為一間臨牀階段的生物科技公司，開發精準療法以治療實體腫瘤，並致力於維持器官功能。我們的領先候選藥物bel-sar正在晚期臨牀開發階段，用於治療早期脈絡膜黑色素瘤（定義為小型脈絡膜黑色素瘤及/或無法確定的病竈）患者，同時也在進行其他眼癌及膀胱癌的臨牀開發。

由於現行標準治療（SoC）的限制，以及患者對放射治療（包括貼片式放射治療或質子束治療）的抗拒，對於脈絡膜黑色素瘤患者而言，有顯著未被滿足的治療需求。這兩種治療方式皆為高度侵入性療法，會導致顯著視力喪失，甚至可能造成治療眼的永久性視力喪失。另一種治療選擇為眼球摘除（Enucleation），即移除受影響的眼球，患者將完全失去視力，且無法恢復視力。我們正在評估bel-sar作為一種視力保留療法的安全性與有效性，以進行我們持續進行的全球第三期CoMpass試驗，用於治療早期脈絡膜黑色素瘤成人患者的首線治療。此外，我們有意評估bel-sar在治療其他種類實體腫瘤的潛力，首先從脈絡膜轉移及膀胱癌開始，因為bel-sar正在這些領域進行臨牀開發，以及眼表癌症。

Bel-sar在臨牀試驗中已顯示臨牀效益，且迄今被認為耐受性良好。在一個第二期試驗（ClinicalTrials.gov ID: NCT04417530）中，評估bel-sar經脈絡膜上皮（SC）給藥方式，用於治療早期脈絡膜黑色素瘤的首線治療，患者在十二個月的追蹤期間被密切監測，以評估腫瘤控制、視力保留及腫瘤生長速率。總共有22位患者參與該試驗。Bel-sar在第三期資格患者中達成80%的腫瘤控制率（n=8/10），其中反應者在接受治療後完全停止生長（反應者治療後平均生長速率為0.011 mm/yr，與試驗入組前的0.351 mm/yr相比；p<0.0001）。這些十位患者中有90%達成視力保留。重要的是，這十位患者中有80%屬於高風險羣，因腫瘤接近視網膜中央或視神經盤，這突顯了這種新型藥物在視力保留方面的潛力。Bel-sar在所有參與者中，無論劑量如何，其安全性表現都非常良好。我們認為第二期試驗的結果是重大成就，考慮到脈絡膜黑色素瘤是一種罕見且危及生命的視網膜癌症，目前尚無核准的視力保留治療方式。我們認為bel-sar有潛力改變眼癌及泌尿系統癌症及其他實體腫瘤的現有治療模式，並正在擴展臨牀開發至另外兩個適應症：脈絡膜轉移及眼表癌症。我們持續在進行脈絡膜轉移的第二期臨牀試驗，並即將啟動眼表癌症的首期概念驗證試驗。
病毒類藥物連結物（VDCs）是一種新型藥物，具有雙重作用機制，能透過將細胞毒性載荷送達癌細胞以產生急性壞死，並啟動二次免疫介導反應，促進癌細胞死亡。Bel-sar為我們的領先VDC候選藥物，由人類乳頭瘤病毒（HPV）的修改過的衣殼蛋白連結至數百個光激活分子所組成。

Bel-sar的光激活設計旨在實現精準的腫瘤細胞殺傷，同時對周圍健康組織造成最小損害。在未激活bel-sar或其與腫瘤細胞膜結合的情況下，不會產生細胞毒性效果。在單次bel-sar劑量後進行多次光激活，會因腫瘤的再氧合及bel-sar的光穩定性而增加抗腫瘤活性。最後，急性壞死會引發免疫原性細胞死亡，進而產生適應性、長期的抗腫瘤免疫反應。VDCs的腫瘤靶向特異性由病毒類粒子（VLPs）對特定修改過的腫瘤相關糖胺聚糖（GAGs）的選擇性結合所驅動，這些GAGs是肝素硫酸蛋白聚醣（HSPGs）的肝素硫酸鏈的一部分，表達在腫瘤細胞膜上。這種靶向機制使bel-sar能夠將多種類型的細胞毒性載荷直接送達廣泛的實體腫瘤。

除了眼癌，bel-sar也在膀胱癌的臨牀開發階段。膀胱癌是全球第九大常見癌症，大多數病例在早期被診斷為非肌肉侵襲性膀胱癌（NMIBC），美國每年約有80,000例病例。儘管早期診斷，NMIBC患者仍具有高風險的復發與進展，現行標準治療（SoC）的療效有限。2025年，我們宣佈在NMIBC的首期試驗（NCT05483868）中取得正面數據。基於首期試驗的正面結果，我們正在推進bel-sar在NMIBC的臨牀開發。我們正在進行NMIBC的首期b/二期試驗，評估更多劑量與治療週期，針對中度及高風險NMIBC患者。
我們的願景是創新癌症治療的未來，以治癒患者並維持器官功能。我們正在開發bel-sar用於多種眼癌適應症，目標是治療腫瘤、維持視力並預防失明。我們的首個適應症為一個潛在的數十億美元市場機會。我們也在評估bel-sar在泌尿系統癌症適應症中的應用，首先在膀胱癌，這是每名患者治療成本最高的癌症之一。預計到2032年，全球膀胱癌市場規模將超過8.0十億美元。
我們的初步重點在眼癌及泌尿系統癌症，這兩個領域皆為高未被滿足的醫療需求，局部靶向治療可能實現早期幹預，如我們的產品線所示。

我們預期在眼癌與泌尿道癌之外，還有其他腫瘤治療領域的發展潛力。

我們的管理團隊包含具備豐富生物科技經驗的產業高階主管，專門於開發與商業化腫瘤與眼科藥物。Elisabet de los Pinos, Ph.D.，我們的首席執行官，曾領導Alimta®在美國禮來公司（Eli Lilly and Company）的市場策略與歐洲商業化，用於治療肺癌。我們的首席醫療官暨研究與發展部門總裁J. Jill Hopkins, M.D. 是一名眼科醫生與視網膜專科醫師，擁有超過30年的眼科經驗，包括擔任諾華藥品（Novartis AG，或簡稱Novartis）全球眼科與探索性開發高級副總裁，以及Gyroscope Therapeutics，一家諾華公司，的首席執行官，當時她負責全球眼科藥物研發路線圖。Anthony Gibney，我們的首席財務與業務官，是一位經驗豐富的生物科技領導者與前投資銀行家，擁有超過30年的經驗，專注於領導與顧問生物科技公司在其業務各方面的發展，包括企業策略、業務拓展、財務與投資者關係等。在他投資銀行生涯後，他曾擔任Achillion Pharmaceuticals, Inc.與Iveric Bio, Inc.的首席業務官，以及Fog Pharmaceuticals, Inc.的首席業務與財務官。Conor Kilroy，我們的首席法律官與祕書，曾在Neurogastrx, Inc.擔任總法律顧問與祕書，時間為2021年9月至2023年5月。Kilroy先生也在Ironwood Pharmaceuticals, Inc.（Nasdaq: IRWD）擔任越來越重要的職務，時間為2013年6月至2021年2月，自2020年4月起擔任高級副總裁、總法律顧問與祕書，自2019年4月起擔任副總裁、總法律顧問與祕書。在他職業生涯早期，Kilroy先生曾在Boston Scientific Corporation與Goodwin Procter LLP的企業法部門擔任職務。Mark Plavsic, Ph.D. 是我們的首席技術官，擁有30年的全球生物科技經驗，包括美國、歐洲與澳洲的端到端技術運作，以及成功將複雜生物製品從臨牀前開發階段轉化為商業化上市與分銷。他先前曾擔任Fate Therapeutics, Inc.與Lysogene的首席技術官。我們相信我們管理團隊的廣度與深度的經驗，將有助於我們推進bel-sar的臨牀與開發策略，並在獲得批准後進行商業化。我們董事會主席David Johnson 是一位生物科技產業資深人士，擁有超過25年的藥物開發經驗。Johnson先生目前是Solve Therapeutics, Inc.的首席執行官與創辦人，這是一家開發新一代mAb基抗癌藥物的生物科技公司。在創辦Solve Therapeutics之前，他曾擔任VelosBio Inc.的首席執行官，這家腫瘤公司於2020年被默克藥品（Merck & Co.）以27.5億美元收購。他也曾擔任Acerta Pharma的首席執行官，該公司被阿斯利康（AstraZeneca）以70億美元收購。Johnson先生擁有領導開發首創性癌症治療藥物的豐富經驗，並對最終獲得監管批准的藥物做出重大貢獻，包括硼替佐米（Velcade®）、羅米地辛（Istodax®）、依達拉錫（Zydelig®）與阿卡替尼（Calquence®）。
在Aura Biosciences，我們的願景是創新癌症照護的未來，以治療病人並維護器官功能，初期重點為眼科與泌尿道癌症。我們實現此目標的關鍵策略要素包括：

▪ 完成bel-sar的全球第三期CoMpass試驗，作為早期脈絡黑色素瘤的第一線治療，並追求美國食品藥物管理局（FDA）的批准。若獲得批准，這將代表首個用於早期脈絡黑色素瘤的治療方式，作為潛在的第一線治療選項，保留放射治療作為第二線治療選項。若獲得批准，我們看到bel-sar在脈絡黑色素瘤的獨立商業化潛力，該疾病每年在美國與歐洲診斷出約11,000名患者。美國與歐洲約有50名眼科腫瘤學家，代表一個聚焦的接觸點，為我們公司提供機會在全球範圍內以專注的銷售團隊來掌握市場價值。

▪ 擴展bel-sar在其他眼科腫瘤適應症的開發，包括轉移至脈絡的腫瘤與眼表癌症。我們相信bel-sar的雙重作用機制有潛力治療腫瘤同時維護關鍵的眼部結構，在影響大量患者的其他眼科癌症中。我們持續在轉移至脈絡的腫瘤的進行中第二期臨牀試驗中納入患者。轉移至脈絡的腫瘤在美國與歐洲的年發病率為20,000名患者。此外，我們計畫進行bel-sar在眼表癌症的第1期概念驗證試驗，包括黑色素瘤與鱗狀細胞癌，該疾病在美國與歐洲的年發病率為35,000名患者，根據眼科腫瘤學界對開發更好治療選擇的強烈興趣。

病毒類藥物偶聯物，或 VDCs，是一種新型藥物，具有雙重作用機制，能透過將細胞毒性載荷送達癌細胞以產生急性壞死，並啟動二次免疫介導反應來促進癌細胞死亡。Bel-sar，我們的領先 VDC 候選藥物，是由人類乳頭瘤病毒，或 HPV，的修改後的衣殼蛋白偶聯至數百個光活化分子所組成。
Bel-sar 的光活化設計旨在實現精確的癌細胞殺傷，同時對周圍健康組織造成最小損害。在 absence of bel-sar 活化或與癌細胞膜結合的情況下，不會產生細胞毒性效果。多次光活化，接續單劑 bel-sar 的給藥，會增加抗腫瘤活性，這是因為

腫瘤的再氧合及 bel-sar 的光穩定性。最後，急性壞死會引發免疫原性細胞死亡，進而產生適應性、長期的抗腫瘤免疫反應。VDCs 的腫瘤靶向特異性是由病毒類粒子，或 VLPs，選擇性結合至某個子集的修改後的腫瘤相關糖胺聚糖，或 GAGs，所驅動，這些 GAGs 是肝素硫酸蛋白聚糖，或 HSPGs，的肝素硫酸鏈的一部分，表達在腫瘤細胞膜上。這種靶向機制使多種類型的細胞毒性載荷能夠直接送達廣泛的實體腫瘤。

除眼癌外，bel-sar 正在膀胱癌的臨牀開發階段。膀胱癌是全球第九常見的癌症，且大多數病例在早期被診斷為非肌肉侵襲性膀胱癌，或 NMIBC，美國每年約有 80,000 個病例。儘管早期診斷，NMIBC 患者仍具有高風險的復發與進展，現有標準治療方式無法有效控制。2025 年，我們宣佈在 NMIBC 的 Phase 1 試驗（NCT05483868）中獲得正面數據。基於已完成 Phase 1 試驗的正面結果，我們正在推進 bel-sar 在 NMIBC 的臨牀開發。我們目前進行 Phase 1b/2 試驗，評估在中度及高風險 NMIBC 患者中追加劑量與療程。

我們於 2009 年在特拉華州成立為一家公司，總部位於麻薩諸塞州波士頓。自成立以來，我們的重點在於識別與開發潛在產品候選藥物、進行預臨牀研究與臨牀試驗、組織與僱用公司員工、業務規劃、建立與維護智慧財產權組合、籌集資金、進行研究與開發活動，以及提供一般及行政支援。截至目前為止，我們尚未有任何產品候選藥物獲准銷售，也尚未產生任何營業收入。我們主要透過發行可轉換優先股、普通股與認購權證來資助營運。自成立至 2025 年 12 月 31 日為止，我們已透過私募發行本公司股票與可轉換優先股，以及發行普通股，共籌得約 498.1 百萬美元的總資金。2025 年 5 月 16 日，我們發行並出售 11,735,565 張普通股、預先資助權證以購買最多 3,571,435 張普通股，以及附屬權證以購買總計 3,826,750 張普通股，或稱為 2025 年追加發行。普通股與預先資助權證在 2025 年追加發行中與附屬普通股權證一同出售，每出售一張普通股或預先資助權證，附屬普通股權證可購買 0.25 張普通股。每張普通股的總發行價格為 4.90 美元，每張預先資助權證的總發行價格為 4.89999 美元。扣除經紀折扣與佣金及發行費用後，我們從 2025 年追加發行中獲得約 69.9 百萬美元的淨資金。2023 年 11 月 9 日，我們發行並出售 11,000,000 張普通股，每張價格為 9.00 美元，總計籌得 99.0 百萬美元，或稱為 2023 年追加發行。扣除經紀折扣與佣金及發行費用後，我們從 2023 年追加發行中獲得約 92.6 百萬美元的淨資金。2022 年 12 月 5 日，我們發行並出售 7,705,000 張普通股，包括經紀人選擇權全額行使後的額外股份，每張價格為 12.00 美元，總計籌得 92.5 百萬美元，或稱為 2022 年追加發行。扣除經紀折扣、佣金及發行費用後，我們從 2022 年追加發行中獲得約 86.7 百萬美元的淨資金。2022 年 11 月 1 日，我們向美國證券交易委員會（SEC）提交了 Form S-3 的存倉註冊聲明（或稱為 2022 年存倉），用以註冊最多總發行價格為 250.0 百萬美元的普通股、優先股、債務證券、權證與單位或其組合。我們同時與 Jefferies LLC（或稱為銷售經紀人）簽訂了 Open Market Sale AgreementSM（或稱為銷售協議），用以提供在「市場現貨」發行（ATM）下，根據銷售協議的條款，發行、發行及出售最多總計 75.0 百萬美元的普通股。在 2023 年追加發行期間，2023 年 11 月 6 日，我們通知 Jefferies LLC 暫停並終止 ATM 發行相關的發行說明書。在 2023 年 12 月 31 日結業年度，我們透過 ATM 發行總計 261,807 張普通股，加權平均價格為 12.49 美元，總計籌得 3.3 百萬美元。2024 年 3 月 27 日，我們向 SEC 提交了新的存倉註冊聲明，Form S-3（或稱為 2024 年存倉），用以註冊最多總發行價格為 350.0 百萬美元的普通股、優先股、債務證券、權證與單位或其組合，此聲明取代了 2022 年存倉。2024 年存倉包含一份發行說明書，用以在銷售協議下進行 ATM 發行。在 2025 年 12 月 31 日結業年度，我們透過 ATM 發行 1,055,362 張普通股，加權平均價格為 6.36 美元，總計籌得 6.7 百萬美元。

自 2009 年成立以來，我們每年均產生重大營運虧損，且尚未產生任何營業收入。我們預期在可預見的未來，仍將持續產生重大費用與營運虧損。我們能否產生足夠的產品收入以實現盈利，將取決於我們產品候選藥物的開發與商業化成功。我們的淨虧損為 106.2 百萬美元與 86.9 百萬美元，分別為 2025 年與 2024 年結業年度。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，我們累計虧損為 480.4 百萬美元。此外，我們的營運虧損可能因臨牀試驗的進行時間與其他研究與開發活動的支出而大幅波動。
我們預期，隨著我們持續進行產品候選藥物的預臨牀研究與臨牀試驗，我們的費用與資金需求將大幅增加。此外，我們作為上市公司運作的相關成本也會增加。我們預期，如果我們進行以下活動，費用與資金需求將大幅增加：
▪ 進行 bel-sar 的現有及未來臨牀試驗； ▪ 推進新適應症的預臨牀與臨牀開發；
▪ 建立製造能力，包括建立與發展合同開發與製造關係；

headings: 與本公司財務狀況相關的風險，以及額外資金需求
自本公司成立以來，我們已產生顯著的淨虧損，並預期在可預見的未來，我們將持續產生虧損，這對我們持續經營的能力構成風險。
我們的會計師已出具「持續經營」審計意見。
近期資本市場的波動可能影響我們透過發行普通股股票或發行負債來取得新資金的能力。
籌集額外資金可能導致現有股東的股權稀釋，限制我們的營運，或要求我們放棄對我們技術或產品候選藥物的專有權利。
與我們產品候選藥物的發現和開發相關的風險
我們高度依賴 bel-sar 的成功，這是截至目前為止我們唯一的產品候選藥物。
我們已啟動但尚未完成關鍵臨牀試驗，也尚未商業化任何藥物產品，這可能使評估我們未來前景變得困難。
若我們未能開發其他產品候選品項，或未能取得第一個產品候選品項的更多適應症證據，則我們的商業機會可能受到限制。
Bel-sar 是一種生物製劑，需要使用多種醫療器材，這可能會導致額外的法規風險。
產品候選品項製造方法或配方的變更，可能會導致額外成本或延遲。
若我們在臨牀試驗中遭遇患者招募的延遲或困難，則我們取得必要的法規核准可能會延遲或無法實現。
動物實驗及早期臨牀試驗的結果，可能無法預測未來的結果。
我們可能會產生額外成本或遭遇延遲，於啟動或完成，或最終無法完成產品候選品項的開發與商業化。
paragraphs: 投資本公司的普通股涉及高度風險。您應仔細閱讀並考慮下列所有風險，以及本年度報告表10-K中其他資訊，包括我們的合併財務報表及其相關附註，以及標題為「管理層對財務狀況與營運結果之討論與分析」的章節。下列所描述的任何事件或發展發生，都可能對我們的業務、財務狀況、營運結果與成長前景造成損害。除非另有說明，本文件中提及本公司業務受損的風險因素，將包括對本公司業務、聲譽、財務狀況、營運結果與未來前景的損害。在這種情況下，本公司普通股的市場價格可能下跌，您可能損失全部或部分投資。此外，尚有其他風險與不確定性，目前我們尚未知悉或認為不重要，也可能影響我們的業務營運與本公司普通股的市場價格。

投資生物科技產品開發具有高度風險，因為這類投資需要大量的前期資金支出，且產品候選藥物可能無法獲得監管機構批准或無法成為商業上可行的產品。我們的淨虧損為2025年12月31日結業年度為106.2百萬美元，2024年12月31日結業年度為86.9百萬美元。截至2025年12月31日，我們累計虧損為480.4百萬美元。我們的淨虧損幾乎全部來自與我們研究與開發計畫相關的支出，以及與我們營運相關的一般及行政費用。我們預期研究與開發費用將隨著我們持續進行bel-sar的臨牀開發，以及持續發現與開發其他產品候選藥物而顯著增加。此外，若我們獲得產品候選藥物的監管批准，我們將產生大量的銷售、市場推廣與製造費用。我們會產生與作為上市公司營運相關的成本，並會產生額外的成本。因此，我們預期將持續產生大量且不斷增加的營運虧損，至少在可預見的未來。由於開發藥物產品涉及許多風險與不確定性，我們無法預測未來虧損的程度或我們何時能實現盈利，如果有的話。截至目前為止，我們尚未從任何產品銷售中產生任何收入。我們的虧損歷史與無收入的狀況，使我們未來持續營運的風險更高。我們實現盈利的能力取決於我們能否產生收入。我們目前尚無任何產品獲得商業銷售批准，因此從來未從產品銷售中產生任何收入，且在可預見的未來也不預期會有。此外，我們預期不會從產品銷售中產生任何收入，直到我們獲得某產品候選藥物商業銷售的市場批准，如果有的話。我們產生收入與實現盈利的能力，很大程度上取決於我們達成多項目標的成功，包括：
▪ 啟動並完成bel-sar在早期脈絡膜黑色素瘤及其它腫瘤適應症（包括脈絡膜轉移及膀胱癌）的研究，以及bel-sar在這些適應症的臨牀前與臨牀開發，以及來自我們VDC技術平台的任何其他研究計畫與未來產品候選藥物的開發；
▪ 獲得bel-sar及任何未來產品候選藥物的市場批准，這些產品候選藥物我們已完成臨牀試驗；
▪ 將我們的製造流程轉移至，並與CDMO合作開發與維護bel-sar及任何未來產品候選藥物的製造流程，包括與第三方建立並維持商業上可行的供應與製造關係；
▪ 發起並商業化bel-sar及任何未來產品候選藥物，我們獲得市場批准後，無論是直接或透過合作夥伴或經銷商。
